what: Why the naive slope is biased
title: Persistence meta-regression with ghreg
text: Write observed effect sizes true effects plus sampling error, \delta_{t} = \theta_{t} + e_{t}, true effects related \theta_2 = \alpha + \beta\theta_1 + \eta. sampling errors correlated \rho, least-squares slope \delta_2 \delta_1 converges \beta plus \underbrace{\frac{\rho\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(e_1)\mathrm{Var}(e_2)}}{\mathrm{Var}(\theta_1) + \mathrm{Var}(e_1)}}_{\text{correlation-driven bias}} \; - \; \underbrace{\frac{\beta\,\mathrm{Var}(e_1)}{\mathrm{Var}(\theta_1) + \mathrm{Var}(e_1)}}_{\text{attenuation bias}}. \rho = 0 familiar attenuation measurement error predictor. difference means constant treatment effect, \rho equals correlation outcome across time (test-retest reliability), typically well zero. \rho > \beta two sampling variances similar, correlation term wins naive slope overstates persistence. standard errors--variables correction, assumes \rho = 0, makes things worse.

title: Persistence meta-regression with ghreg
text: pair j study k, \begin{aligned} \theta_{1jk} &= \mu + u_{1k} + \epsilon_{1jk}, \\ \theta_{2jk} &= \alpha + \beta\,\theta_{1jk} + u_{2k} + \epsilon_{2jk}, \\ \begin{pmatrix}\delta_{1jk} \\ \delta_{2jk}\end{pmatrix} &\sim N\!\left(\begin{pmatrix}\theta_{1jk} \\ \theta_{2jk}\end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix}\mathrm{se}_{1jk}^2 & \rho_{jk}\,\mathrm{se}_{1jk}\,\mathrm{se}_{2jk} \\ \rho_{jk}\,\mathrm{se}_{1jk}\,\mathrm{se}_{2jk} & \mathrm{se}_{2jk}^2\end{pmatrix}\right), \end{aligned} u_{1k} \sim N(0, \sigma_{S1}^2), u_{2k} \sim N(0, \sigma_{S2}^2), \epsilon_{1jk} \sim N(0, \sigma_{E1}^2), \epsilon_{2jk} \sim N(0, \sigma_{E2}^2). four SDs reported study_sd1, study_sd2, es_sd1, es_sd2: S (study) -study level E (effect size) level effect-size pairs within studies. two-level model one level heterogeneity, reported study_sd1 study_sd2: paper’s \tau_1 \tau_2. \beta links true effects within studies. study effects u_{1k} u_{2k} capture clustering true effects within studies. sampling errors different pairs assumed independent, even within study. study reports several effect sizes participants, sampling errors likely correlated well, model account . Rather sampling every latent effect, Stan program integrates \theta, \epsilon, u analytically. pair contributes 2 \times 2 block study rank-2 correction, handled Woodbury identity. posterior latent-variable program paper’s appendix, Stan samples seven hyperparameters. makes fits fast avoids funnel geometry causes divergent transitions sampling error large relative heterogeneity.

title: Simulate a persistence meta-analysis — gh_simulate
text: Outcomes unit variance within arm, effect sizes standardized scale. Participants split evenly arms. true effects follow model gh_reg(): $$\theta_{1jk} = \mu + u_{1k} + \epsilon_{1jk}$$ $$\theta_{2jk} = \alpha + \beta \theta_{1jk} + u_{2k} + \epsilon_{2jk}$$ study effects \(u_{1k} \sim N(0, \sigma_{S1}^2)\) \(u_{2k} \sim N(0, \sigma_{S2}^2)\) shared every pair study \(k\), pair-level deviations \(\epsilon_{1jk} \sim N(0, \sigma_{E1}^2)\) \(\epsilon_{2jk} \sim N(0, \sigma_{E2}^2)\). arguments study_sd1, study_sd2, es_sd1, es_sd2 set \(\sigma_{S1}\), \(\sigma_{S2}\), \(\sigma_{E1}\), \(\sigma_{E2}\), names output gh_reg(). default study contributes one pair, data follow two-level model, heterogeneity set study level (study_sd1 = 0.25, es_sd1 = 0). matches gh_reg(), reports two-level model's SDs study_sd1 study_sd2: one pair per study, total SD time identified, two-level fit estimates \(\sqrt{\sigma_{S1}^2 + \sigma_{E1}^2}\) whichever level put variation . simulate data three-level model, give studies several pairs (pairs_per_study set pair-level SDs es_sd1 es_sd2 0. pair simulated trial, sampling errors independent across pairs, including pairs study. real meta-analyses, several effect sizes one study often share participants, sampling errors correlated; neither gh_simulate() gh_reg() models .
